title: Solve a line–quadratic system algebraically
subtitle: Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  · 26 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **26 of the official questions in Nonlinear equations in one variable and systems of equations in two variables  are this one** — 7 Easy, 9 Medium, 10 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Hard tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Two equations are given with no graph, one linear and one quadratic, or one that gives y directly.
- The question asks which ordered pair is a solution, or for a value of x, y or a combination of them at the intersection.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Substitute the expression for y, or for the simpler variable, into the other equation.
- 2) Solve the resulting quadratic in one variable by factoring out a common factor or using the formula.
- 3) Put each x back into the simpler equation to get y.
- With choices, testing each ordered pair in both equations can be faster.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Type both equations and click the intersection points to read the ordered pairs directly.
This is usually the fastest route on multiple choice.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You find x but then report a pair whose y came from the wrong equation, or you pick a pair that satisfies only one equation.
Dividing by x instead of factoring it out also loses the x = 0 solution.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You find x but then report a pair whose y came from the wrong equation, or you pick a pair that satisfies only one equation.
Dividing by x instead of factoring it out also loses the x = 0 solution.
